# Test data

Every file under `testdata/` is our own material, licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 like the rest of the repository (© Recursive AI, LLC).

- The audio files are deterministic synthetic signals (sines, noise, clicks) generated by the scripts in `tools/` and, where a format
  needs an outside encoder, encoded with that encoder run as a black-box command-line tool (`flac`, LAME, ffmpeg's libvorbis and
  libopus). Nothing from those tools is included beyond the encoded output of our own signals.
  - `wav/`: `tools/gen_wav_seeds.py`
  - `flac/`: `tools/gen_flac_seeds.py`
  - `mp3/`: `tools/gen-mp3-testset.py`
  - `opus/`: `tools/gen-opus-testdata.sh`
  - `containers/`: `tools/gen-container-testdata.sh` (MP4/M4A/3GP/ADTS via ffmpeg; AMR frames from `tools/gen-amr-testdata.py`, whose payloads are
    pseudo-random bytes of the right sizes, not speech; `tools/add-itunsmpb.py` adds the iTunes gapless tag)
  - `transients/`: `tools/gen-transient-testdata.py` (see its README)
- `fuzz/`: small inputs that once crashed or misled a parser, minimised from our own seeds.

Third-party test vectors and corpora (Opus, Vorbis, FLAC, MP3, AAC and AMR conformance material and EBU loudness material) are not committed;
`tools/fetch-corpus.sh` (and `tools/fetch-aac-conformance.sh` for the AAC streams) downloads them by pinned URL and SHA-256.
